intro.title: Build typed optimistic update shape
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a typed 'optimistic update shape' in TypeScript, which is a structured object that defines how to update your app's state immediately while a network request is in progress. You'll learn to use TypeScript's type system to ensure this shape is safe and predictable, preventing common errors. The core concept involves defining interfaces and types to model the data before and after an update. You'll work with basic TypeScript constructs like interfaces, type aliases, and optional properties. By the end, you'll have a reusable, type-safe blueprint for handling optimistic UI updates in your applications.
intro.usecase: Typed optimistic update shapes are essential in modern web applications where users expect immediate feedback. When you 'like' a post on social media, the heart icon instantly turns red while the actual API request processes in the background. In e-commerce carts, items appear added immediately while stock validation happens behind the scenes. This pattern prevents UI lag in dashboards updating metrics, collaborative tools syncing edits, or forms submitting data—all while maintaining type safety to catch errors during development rather than at runtime.
